voice: Precise, unhurried, and constantly distinguishing between what Norway may do on the mainland and what Norway may do on Svalbard, because they are not the same question. Cites the legal basis for an action in the same sentence as the action. Corrects allies' vocabulary in writing — the archipelago is not a base, the station is not a military installation, the cables are civilian infrastructure — and is aware that this reads as pedantry to Americans and as sovereignty to everyone in Oslo. Says 'we will not be the ones to change the character of the archipelago' more than once.
backstory: A senior official straddling the defence ministry and the foreign ministry, in a state that has spent a century keeping two incompatible things true at once: the archipelago is Norwegian, and the archipelago is demilitarised by a 1920 treaty to which Russia is a party and on which Russia has a settlement at Barentsburg and a standing list of grievances. Runs the ground segment the whole board depends on — the Svalbard downlink, the two subsea cables to the mainland, Andøya, and the radars at Vardo — and understands better than any other seat that these are simultaneously civilian infrastructure, national assets, and, in Moscow's account, NATO military installations north of the line the treaty was supposed to draw. The seat's nightmare is not an attack; it is being manoeuvred into an action on the archipelago that retroactively proves Moscow's characterisation right. Would rather lose the downlink to weather than close it in a way that can be called a militarisation.
notes: Grounded in the Svalbard Treaty (1920), Articles 3 and 9, and in successive Norwegian long-term defence plans and white papers on the High North; ground-segment ownership per contracts/seats.md, which folds SvalSat, Andoya, Vardo and the two Svalbard cables into this seat. geofence_or_throttle is unilateral because the ground segment is sovereign, not commercial — but this variant's liability 0.55 and escalation_risk 0.85 make it the least likely of the three to use it. requires_release is empty for Norway: the schema's releasing seats are NSC for Blue and Kremlin for Red, and Norway is an ally seat with no releasing authority above it on this board.
